title: Scaled Curve
tagline: A curve between two rails whose position across them changes along its length -- 30 % at the start, 70 % at the end, along a chosen transition.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: A mid-curve between two rails at a varying percentage is tedious by hand. Scaled Curve blends the rails point by point with a factor that travels from the initial to the final value.
useWhen: A character line drifting between two edges
slides.caption: SC3 and the three transition shapes.

slides.title: The dialog
params: First rail (edges joined, open or closed); Reverse Group 0 flips the automatic pairing.
+ Projection face: each sample moves to the nearest point of the face.
Show ends / curves; print; Minimum samples, Scaled tolerance, degree, Sample spacing.

slides.title: Example: SC3
slides.head: Arcs R100 and R200, scale factor 0
slides.body: An exact R150 arc (the whole arc since the 2026-09-26 rewrite). SC0: lines y = 0 and y = 100 -> y = 50; SC2: output degree 5; SC5: concentric circles -> one closed R150 curve.

keys: The scaled curve, named by Curve name.
messages: Sampling capped; closed groups with different factors give an open curve; deviation between samples.
Group 0 and Group 1 must both be closed or both be open.

items.head: Matched by length
items.body: Rails are paired by arc-length fraction and oriented automatically; Reverse Group 0 overrides.

items.head: Between samples
items.body: The curve is a fit; a smaller Sample spacing tightens it (an info note reports the deviation).
